An Early History of International Students at Northbridge

Posted on 4 March 2021. Filed under campus history.

The first international students arrived at Northbridge in 1894, travelling for six weeks by sea. Their letters home describe a campus of four buildings and one very cold library.

The 1920s cohort

By 1925 international students made up a tenth of the entering class. Most came from three countries, and most returned home to teach.

Endowment history

A bequest in 1948 established the college's first endowed scholarship fund, which at the time supported four students a year in the study of metallurgy.
